about: Synthetic data. Marina is a fictional person; every capsule was written for this demo.

capsules.text: Hi 23-year-old me. I'm 18, it's the first week of engineering at UTFPR and I already miss drawing in class instead of paying attention. Mom says illustration is a hobby, not a job, so here I am, calculus at 7:30am. Promise me two things: you will keep drawing, at least one page a week, and you will finally learn to swim. It's embarrassing to live in Brazil, dream about the sea every night, and not know how to swim. Also: call Vó Lúcia every Sunday. She pretends she doesn't care, but she waits by the phone.

New Year's Eve in Matinhos with Bia and the whole family. Vó Lúcia fell asleep at 11:40 and still swore she saw the fireworks. I stood with my feet in the water at midnight because that's as far as I go. I want to live somewhere I can see the sea from the window. Ten years from now: do you? Is Bia still the first person you text? I hope the answer to both is yes.

I failed Cálculo 1. I'm writing this crying in the RU so that next year you remember it wasn't the end of the world. Rafa bought me a pastel and said I'm too smart to fail twice. He's annoying and I think I love him. Also, I haven't drawn in two months. I know. I know.

Rafa, if you're reading this, we made it five years. You said capsules are cheesy, so this is me being cheesy on purpose. Thank you for the playlist that got me through Física 2, for learning Vó Lúcia's bolo de fubá recipe just to impress her, and for not laughing (much) when I panicked in the swimming pool. Whatever happens, I hope we're still the kind of people who dance in the kitchen.

Passei em Cálculo 1, finalmente. And something new: I started drawing little comics about the bus line Interbairros and posting them. 300 people follow them now. Strangers recognize the old man with the parrot from the 7am bus. I don't know what this is but it feels more like me than anything in the course. Future me, did you keep the comics going? Please don't have deleted the account in a bad mood.

Internship at a factory in CIC. I measure vibrations in motors. It's fine. The engineers are kind and I'm good at it, which is the scary part, because being good at something you don't love is a trap. I stopped the bus comics in January, there's no time. Vó Lúcia got sick in February, pneumonia, she's better now. I called every Sunday and some Wednesdays too.

Rafa and I broke up last week. Nobody did anything wrong, we just want different cities: he wants São Paulo, I want the sea. I'm writing this so in a year you remember it was the right call even though it hurts now. I kept the playlist. I'm not ready to delete it.

Graduated! Vó Lúcia came to the ceremony with a hat bigger than her and clapped at the wrong name twice. Got a job offer from the same factory. I said yes. I keep telling myself it's for two years, then I go somewhere by the sea. Writing it here so it becomes a promise: two years, Marina.

Bia, you moved to Florianópolis today and I'm already jealous of your window. Thank you for 15 years of friendship, for the sleepovers when I failed Cálculo, for telling me Rafa wasn't the end of the world, and for being the only person who still asks me 'are you drawing?'. When you read this, I'll probably be there visiting. Save me the room facing the sea.

Pandemic. Working from my bedroom. I can't visit Vó Lúcia, so I call her every day now and she complains that it's too much and then talks for an hour. I started drawing again because there's nothing else to do: small drawings of her stories, the farm in Irati, the dog called Coronel. She doesn't know. I want to give her a little book when this is over.

Vó Lúcia died on Tuesday. Covid. We couldn't be in the room. I didn't finish the book in time. I'm writing this because in ten years I want to remember her laugh exactly, not just that she laughed: it started high and fell like stairs. She called me 'menina do mar'. I will finish the book. I promise you I will finish it.

I stopped calling anyone on Sundays because there's no one to call on Sundays anymore, and that sentence is the saddest thing I've written. Therapy started. The therapist asked what I would do if I weren't afraid. I said: draw for a living and live near the sea. She asked what I was afraid of. I'm still thinking.

Signed up for swimming lessons. Adult beginners, 7am, I'm the youngest by 20 years. Dona Cida, 71, swims better than me and calls me 'a engenheira'. I swallowed half the pool today. I'm going back Thursday.

I SWAM 25 METERS WITHOUT STOPPING. Dona Cida cried. I cried. 18-year-old me asked for this in 2014 and it took eight years, but it happened. Writing it down so it's official: promise kept. Next one is harder: the factory. It's been almost four years, not two.

Quit the factory. Took a remote job doing technical drawings and diagrams for a solar energy startup, half the salary of being a 'real engineer', twice the happiness. Mom said 'finally something with drawing in it' as if she hadn't told me drawing wasn't a job. I laughed instead of arguing. Growth?

Lisbon! I'm writing this from a café in Alfama, three weeks of working remotely here. I can see the Tejo, which isn't technically the sea but it smells like it. I keep thinking I could live here. Then I think of Bia and Mom and the RU pastel and I'm not sure. Future me: did you move? Don't lie.

Moved to Florianópolis. Not Lisbon, not yet. Bia's spare room really does face the sea, she saved it, like I asked in 2019. I wake up and the window is all blue. I'm 28. 18-year-old me wanted exactly this window. I opened her capsule from New Year's 2014 early by accident and the answer to both of her questions is yes.

Ten years since Matinhos. This year I didn't stay with my feet in the water at midnight, I swam out a little. Bia screamed. I want to write down the people at this New Year's: Bia, her girlfriend Júlia, Mom who came up for the week, Dona Cida's postcard on the fridge. Missing: Vó Lúcia, as always.

I started the book about Vó Lúcia again. I'm calling it 'Menina do Mar'. 12 pages done. It's harder than I thought because every page is a conversation with her and then I need a walk. I'm drawing on Sundays, at the time I used to call her. Feels right.

Ran into Rafa at a friend's wedding in Curitiba. He's married, lives in São Paulo, has a daughter called Lua. We danced one song, in the kitchen of the party venue, as a joke, and it was nice and not sad at all. He still has the playlist too. I deleted mine on the way home. Not out of pain. It just finished.

Opened the capsule from March 2021 today, the one about the therapist asking what I'd do if I weren't afraid. I do both now. Not perfectly: the drawings pay half the bills and the sea is Bia's window, not mine. But I'm not afraid of the answer anymore. Next fear to look at: whether I'm brave enough to publish the book.

'Menina do Mar' is finished. 64 pages. I printed one copy and took it to Vó Lúcia's grave in Irati and read it out loud, which is ridiculous and I don't care. A small publisher in Curitiba wants to see it. I said I'd think about it. Future me: did you say yes?

sensitive_examples.label: To a grandmother who died since
sensitive_examples.context: The recipient's grandmother, Lúcia, passed away in 2020.
sensitive_examples.text: Vó, this is for your 85th birthday! I recorded the whole family singing for you, even Tio Beto who can't sing. Next year we're all going to Irati to see the farm again, you promised to show me where Coronel used to sleep. Te amo, menina do mar.

sensitive_examples.label: To an ex-partner
sensitive_examples.context: The sender and recipient broke up in 2018. He is now married.
sensitive_examples.text: Rafa, if you're reading this, we made it five years. Whatever happens, I hope we're still the kind of people who dance in the kitchen. I can't wait to see what our apartment by the sea looks like.

sensitive_examples.label: A happy reminder
sensitive_examples.text: Hey future me! Today I swam 25 meters without stopping for the first time. Dona Cida cried. Go to the beach today and swim a little, for old times' sake.
